title: Chartwise flat pullback of a blowup and its exceptional fibre
statement:
Let $g:Y\to X$ be a flat morphism of schemes and $\mathcal I$ a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal on $X$, with extended ideal $\mathcal J=\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y$ [def-weil-flat-morphism, pqf-def-coherent, def-nagata-extended-ideal]. Use the ordinary blowups [def-nagata-global-blowup] and the canonical comparison
$$\operatorname{bc}_g:\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J}Y\xrightarrow{\sim}Y\times_X\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}X$$
[def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map]. On affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$ and $\operatorname{Spec}B\subset g^{-1}\operatorname{Spec}A$, write $I=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}A,\mathcal I)$, $J=IB$ and $\varphi:A\to B$. For every generator $a\in I$ the inverse image of the standard chart $\operatorname{Spec}A[I/a]$ is precisely the chart $\operatorname{Spec}B[J/\varphi(a)]$ under this comparison [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring]. Its ring isomorphism is
$$B\otimes_A A[I/a]\xrightarrow{\sim}B[J/\varphi(a)],\qquad b\otimes(c/a)\longmapsto b\varphi(c)/\varphi(a),\quad c\in I$$
[def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. These maps commute with the structural maps, identify the extended centre ideals, and on an overlap with a generator $a'$ identify localization at $a'/a$ with localization at $\varphi(a')/\varphi(a)$. For $y\in Y$, $x=g(y)$, the fibre of the new blowup over $y$ is canonically
$$\bigl(\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}X\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\bigr)\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y),$$
compatibly with these chart maps [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-residue-field]. If $g$ is etale, $x$ is closed and $y$ lies over $x$, and $\mathcal I$ is the ideal sheaf of the reduced closed point $x$, that is, of the closed immersion $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf, def-weil-closed-immersion], there is an open neighbourhood $Y'$ of $y$ for which $\mathcal J|_{Y'}$ is exactly the ideal sheaf of the closed immersion $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)\to Y'$ [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Thus the same chartwise comparison applies to $\operatorname{Bl}_yY'$, with no identification of the two residue fields assumed.

proof.text: Set A=Gamma(X,U), B=Gamma(Y,V), and J=(I.comap g)(V). The affine comap formula of [def-nagata-extended-ideal] identifies J with IB. Use the existing map sigma_a of [def-nagata-strict-chart-to-extended-blowup-chart], with its coefficientwise formula for every pure tensor. It is surjective by [lemma-nagata-strict-chart-map-surjective]. Multiplication by a on A[I/a] is injective: include this subalgebra of A_a [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring] into A_a and cancel the unit a/1. The flatness of B over A, obtained by applying the affine criterion to the given flat scheme morphism, preserves this regular scalar action after tensoring (Mathlib IsSMulRegular.of_flat_of_isBaseChange and TensorProduct.isBaseChange). Hence the a-power torsion of B tensor_A A[I/a] is zero. The kernel formula [lemma-nagata-strict-chart-map-kernel] therefore makes sigma_a injective. AlgEquiv.ofBijective yields e; transport IB=J. Its pure-tensor formula is the defining formula of sigma_a. This construction uses neither a regularity assumption on a in A nor a choice of an unspecified witness.

proof.text: Put rho=bc_g followed by the projection to the old blowup, using [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map]. The projection equation and pullback.condition give new_blowupMap followed by g = rho followed by old_blowupMap. Uniqueness in [thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property], as implemented by blowupι_comp_of_le_preimage, identifies rho on affine blowups with AffineBlowup.hom of the actual appLE map. The homogeneous chart identifications [def-nagata-homogeneous-away-to-chart, lemma-nagata-homogeneous-away-to-chart, lemma-nagata-homogeneous-away-to-chart-injective, lemma-nagata-homogeneous-away-to-chart-surjective] give the fraction charts. The existing isPullback_baseChangeChartι theorem in WeilConjectures.Compactification.StrictTransformChartModel gives their commuting square with sigma_a; its second projection is the required affine chart equality. Tensor induction and the coefficientwise formula identify e with sigma_a. Compose with the global affine chart embedding to obtain the asserted square for the specified bc_g. The identities chartRingιOfEq_toSpec and blowupι_comp_blowupMap give the structural map. By [lem-sfb-proj-map-standard-charts], the inverse image under AffineBlowup.hom of the old generator chart is the new generator chart. The preimage of V under the new blowup map is the range of its affine-open embedding. Using the local comparison square and injectivity of the old affine-open embedding gives exactly range(new fraction chart)=rho^(-1)(range(old fraction chart)) intersect new_blowupMap^(-1)(V).

proof.text: Use Ideal.map_map twice. Since e is a B-algebra equivalence, e composed with A -> B tensor_A A[I/a] equals the composite A -> B -> B[J/b]. Transport along J=IB [def-nagata-extended-ideal]. This proves the centre-ideal equality directly, without choosing principal generators or invoking a separate principalization theorem. The generic calculation is the private proved helper map_ideal_algEquiv.

proof.text: For c in I put t=1 tensor chartGenerator(I,a,c). Localize the actual ring equivalence e at the powers of t using Mathlib IsLocalization.ringEquivOfRingEquiv; Submonoid.map_powers identifies the image submonoid with powers of e(t). The lemma ringEquivOfRingEquiv_mk' gives z/t^n -> e(z)/e(t)^n, and map_pow identifies the denominators. Apply this to each c to obtain the required overlap formula. This is ordinary localization functoriality for a ring equivalence and does not require a homogeneous overlap cocycle theorem.

source.place: Tag 00CO, localization universal property, applied to the chart equivalence of Tag 0BIP

proof.text: Put P = Bl_I X. The canonical comparison bc_g of [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map] is an isomorphism over Y by [thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change]. Therefore its first projection together with the new blowup map forms a pullback square. Apply Mathlib isPullback_fiberToSpecResidueField_of_isPullback to this square at y, retaining the actual residue-field map of [def-weil-residue-field]. Its isoPullback identifies the new fibre with the pullback of the old fibre along Spec of that field map. The isoPullback_hom_fst and isoPullback_hom_snd equations, followed by pullback.lift_fst, prove exactly the two required projection identities. This uses only the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product], and does not depend on the chart assertion.

source.place: Tag 0805 (lemma-flat-base-change-blowing-up), followed by the universal property of fibre products

proof.text: Let F = Y times_X Spec kappa(g(y)), k = g.fiberι (g(y)), and z = g.asFiber y. Since g(y) is closed, its canonical residue-field point is a closed immersion, so k is a closed immersion and ker(k) = I.comap g by [def-nagata-extended-ideal]. The fibre is discrete by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points]. Its map to Spec kappa(g(y)) is etale by base change; hence F is reduced by [etale-proposition-etale-reduced]. The set C = k(F minus {z}) is closed in Y, including for infinite F, because F is discrete and k is a closed embedding. Set V = Y minus C; injectivity of k and k(z)=y give y in V. Lift the canonical point map Spec kappa(y) to i:Spec kappa(y) -> V using its singleton range. The singleton {y} is closed in Y, being the closed image k({z}), so the lift i is a closed immersion by cancellation. Let q:V times_Y F -> V be the first projection. Its source is an open subscheme of reduced F and is reduced, and its range is exactly the singleton represented by y in V. The range of i is the same singleton. The proved source-library identity Scheme.Hom.ker_eq_vanishingIdeal says that a morphism with reduced source has kernel equal to the vanishing ideal of the closure of its range. Applied to q and i it gives ker(q)=ker(i). Finally Mathlib ker_fst_of_isClosedImmersion identifies ker(q) with (I.comap g).comap V.ι, proving the required ideal equality. No identification of residue fields, or selection of a witness from an unproved existence theorem, occurs.
